mainEvent.title: Wed 11/25 · PCE inflation, Q3 GDP, durable goods and jobless claims all land at 8:30a
mainEvent.body: Thanksgiving squeezes the week's data into Wednesday morning. October core PCE, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, is expected to rise **0.3%** on the month and **3.2%** on the year, up from 3.1%, with headline PCE seen at 3.8% from 3.6% (AskTraders, FXEmpire, Newsquawk); Polymarket puts 3.2% at about 58% (Mon 11/23 close). The second estimate of Q3 GDP (advance **3.4%**), October durable goods and jobless claims, moved up a day, come out at the same time, then new home sales at 10:00a and the Fed's Beige Book at 2:00p. A December 9 hike is almost fully priced after last week's hawkish minutes, so a hot print could revive talk of a half-point move, while a soft one would back Treasury Secretary Bessent's Sunday warning against over-tightening. Before that: Dell, HP and Workday report Tuesday after the close. Markets are shut Thursday and close at 1:00p Friday.

stories.title: Nvidia reinstates Huang, and stocks have their best day since April 2025.
stories.body: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director, effective immediately, 11 days after he resigned. Harvey Jones stays as chair and Colette Kress goes back to being CFO only. The board said it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and is confident the move "poses no national security risk", while its independent committee looking into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort "will proceed to conclusion" (Nvidia release, SEC 8-K). "Congratulations to NVIDIA on having made, what I consider to be, an absolutely GREAT decision!" Trump posted (Yahoo Finance). Nvidia rose **31.5%** to **$165.05**, a market value of about $3.98T (FinanceFeeds, Motley Fool). The S&P 500 gained **4.73%** to 7,237.17, the Nasdaq **6.51%** to 24,089.56, the Dow 1,447.98 points (3.01%) to 49,595.31 and the Russell 2000 3.40% to 2,669.66, the best day for the big three since April 2025, ending the S&P's seven-session slide (Motley Fool, FinanceFeeds, Pomegra, ad-hoc-news; Reuters). Dell rose 20.5%, Micron 19%, Intel 16%, TSMC 14%, CoreWeave 22% and Nebius 20%, while Anthropic slipped 1.4%; tech (XLK) gained 9.0% and only energy and staples fell. Nomura's Charlie McElligott called it "a massive surge of MECHANICAL buying" that "guarantees us nothing" (Yahoo Finance). Still open: the SEC accounting review reported Friday, and the 10-Q due Dec 4 (FourWeekMBA).

stories.title: Williams says the Fed still has "work to do" as markets lock in a December hike.
stories.body: "We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis," NY Fed President Williams said Monday. "There is still work to do to get that done." He sees inflation ending 2026 at 3.5%, falling to just above 2% next year and reaching 2% in 2028, with risks "skewed to the upside" (Reuters). Kalshi has a 25bp hike on December 9 at **94%**, a hold at 4% and a bigger hike at 3%; CME FedWatch had about 97% on 25bp as of Friday (Yahoo Finance, BigGo). Short-term yields rose about 7bp, with the 2Y near 4.69%, while the 10Y barely moved at about 4.93% (Reuters, CNBC). The 2-yr auction drew strong direct bidding but soft indirect demand (Reuters). November's flash PMIs cooled: composite 54.6, a four-month low, services 54.7 vs 55.6 expected, manufacturing 54.5 as expected, with cost pressures easing but still elevated (S&P Global via Newsquawk, QNC). On Sunday Treasury Secretary Bessent warned the Fed against over-tightening (CBS). Next: core PCE Wednesday at 8:30a (est 3.2% y/y) and the Beige Book at 2:00p; the pre-meeting blackout starts Saturday.

stories.title: Earnings: HPE guides far above estimates but slips after a 17% run; Dell and HP report Tuesday.
stories.body: Hewlett Packard Enterprise earned **$1.43** a share adjusted vs $1.27–1.29 expected on revenue of **$14.55B** vs $14.35–14.43B; its cloud and AI segment grew 68.6% to $11.26B. It guided Q1 EPS to $1.30–1.40 vs $1.08 expected and revenue to $14.0–14.6B vs $12.84B, raised fiscal 2027 EPS to $5.05–5.35 vs $4.74 and added a $5B buyback, yet the stock fell more than 6% after hours after jumping about 17% in the session (Investing.com, The Fly). Zoom earned $1.59 adjusted vs $1.49 on revenue of $1.29B vs $1.28B and raised its full-year EPS outlook, but its Q4 sales guide was in line and the stock eased 1.2% to $85.10 after hours (StockStory). Agilent's Q4 revenue rose 9.6% to $2.04B with non-GAAP EPS of $1.86, and it guided fiscal 2027 EPS to $6.73–6.86 (SEC 8-K). CrowdStrike closed **−8.9%** at $208.97 and Zscaler **+17.7%** at $229.24, about 3% below the deal's value at CrowdStrike's new price (1.135 × $208.97 ≈ $237) (FinanceFeeds). Tuesday after the close: Dell (guided adjusted EPS of about $6.50 on $49.0B; Polymarket has a beat of $6.71 at about 88%), HP Inc., Workday, Autodesk and Nutanix. Before the open: Analog Devices, Medtronic, Best Buy, Dick's, Dollar Tree, Burlington, Abercrombie and Kohl's; Deere reports Wednesday (StockTitan, FXEmpire).

stories.title: Oil sinks to a three-month low as Libya restarts a pipeline.
stories.body: Brent settled at **$89.37**, down $3.20 (3.5%), its lowest close since Aug 31, and January WTI at **$80.17**, down $3.24 (3.9%), its lowest since Aug 10 (Reuters via OK Energy Today, rallies.ai). Libya's Sharara pipeline has reopened and Middle East supplies rose, outweighing worries about attacks on shipping and refineries in the region. JPMorgan expects prices to fall to the high $70s in the first half of 2027 on a supply surplus. Energy (XLE) fell 1.1%, one of only two sectors down on the day. Brent lost 3.4% last week, its third straight weekly drop, and the IEA sees a surplus of about 2 million barrels a day this quarter (Palma Futures, Bloomberg via Rigzone). OPEC+ meets Nov 29 on 2027 output.

stories.title: Anthropic slips again while the rest of AI rallies, near its $83 IPO price.
stories.body: Anthropic (**ANT**) fell about **1.4%** Monday, its third day of trading, even as Nvidia jumped 31% (Reuters, FinanceFeeds); it was below $88 at 11:00a (Yahoo Finance). It closed Friday about 9% below its $97.17 debut close, after trading as low as $83.05, five cents above the $83 IPO price (FinanceFeeds, TipRanks). It opened at $111.50 on its first trade Thursday. Seaport Research started coverage at Neutral with no price target, citing slowing revenue growth (FinanceFeeds). The deal raised about $93.5B including selling holders, plus a $26B private placement at $83 with Microsoft, Google, Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom (TipRanks). Its fade from the opening print was one of the triggers of last week's AI selloff (AP, Reuters).

stories.title: Asia steps in to steady markets: Taiwan bans short sales, China and Korea ease rules.
stories.body: Taiwan banned short sales below the prior close from Monday and its NT$500B stabilization fund is buying (FSC, Bloomberg via StockAnalysis); China's exchanges cut the minimum margin ratio to 80% from Nov 30; and South Korea readied stabilization funds and eased buyback limits. On Monday the Taiex closed **+2.2%**, but the Kospi fell **3.3%** to 4,708.54 after a 5.8% intraday drop; Hong Kong and Shanghai were flat and Japan was shut (AP, NERO). Reuters' Jamie McGeever said there is "no room for complacency" despite the steps. The Bank of Korea decides Thursday, with a 25bp hike to 3.25% expected (Newsquawk).
